 JUDGMENT This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 24-08-2022 at about 8.30 a.m., the petitioner was walking by the side of the road,
at Melapuram, carefully and cautiously.
At that time the driver of one Tata ACE vehicle bearing No.AP-02-TD-0966, came in reverse direction, in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained multiple injuries to her right leg.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Hindupur Government Hospital,
wherein she took first aid treatment and thereafter, she was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an indoor patient and underwent surgeries.
Earlier to the accident, the petitioner was working as tailor at Zaki Garments, Gowribidanur and was earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
But, due to the above accidental injuries, the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost her earning capacity.
The Hindupur Town Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Tata ACE for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of tata ace goods vehicle bearing No.AP-02-TD-0966 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further, it is contended that, the Mahabunny vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189857663/
2 petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: At the time of accident, the driver of Tata Ace Goods vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

The Tata Ace Goods vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the said vehicle has been falsely implicated by the petitioner in collusion with the owner of said vehicle and the Police, in order to claim compensation.

Further it has contended that, the Tata Ace Goods vehicle was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the said vehicle, the said accident occurred due to the self negligence on the part of the petitioner, who was crossing the road without having proper look out at vehicular movements on the road, without noticing oncoming vehicles she was crossing the road carelessly and sustained injuries due to self fall.

It has further contended that,
the petition is bad for jon-joinder of proper and necessary parties to the petition.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
In view of above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

per month.

10. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.2(a) are true copies of First Information Statement and its translated copy, Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.3(a) are true copies of Station Case Diary Part-II and its translated copy, Ex.P.4 and Ex.P.4(a) are true copies of Sketch and its translated copy, Ex.P.5 is true copy of Wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is true copy of Charge- sheet, Ex.P.8 to Ex.P.10 are Discharge Summaries, Ex.P.11 are Medical Bills (total 103), Ex.P.12 are Prescriptions (total 23),

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, on 24-08- 2022 at about 8.30 a.m., when the petitioner was walking by the side of the road, at Melapuram, carefully and cautiously, the driver of offending Tata ACE vehicle bearing No.AP-02- TD-0966, came in reverse direction, in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner has sustained multiple injuries to her right leg.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge- sheet, marked as Ex.P.7, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the Tata Ace Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-02-TD-0966 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on her right leg.

12. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, issuance of insurance policy in favour of the respondent No.2, with respect to offending Tata Ace Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-02-TD-0966 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

sentences.text: But, the respondent No.1 has no adduced any evidence to establish the said contentions.

Except the self servings statements of the respondent No.1, there is absolutely no evidence placed on record by the respondents to establish the specific contentions taken in the written statements or any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Further, the P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the above contentions suggested in her cross-examination.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or establishes that, there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle and the said accident is caused due to self negligence and self fall of the petitioner.
13. It seems very strange to note that, the respondent No.1 has taken contrary stand in the case.

At one point, in its written statement, the respondent No.1 has taken specific defence that, the Tata Ace Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-02-TD-0966 is not at all involved in the alleged accident and the same has been falsely implicated by the petitioner in the case, in collusion with the respondent No.2 and the Police.

At the other point, in the same written statement, the respondent No.1 has contended that, the alleged accident has occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner, as she was crossing the road carelessly, without having proper look out at vehicular movements of the road and without noticing the on coming vehicles.
Whereas, the offending car was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the car.

14. The Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the extreme left side of 10 feet wide road, situated infront of the house of petitioner, at Melapuram, Hidupur, Rri Satya Sai, Andra-Pradesh, due to dashing of offending Tata ACE Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-02-TD-0966 to the petitioner, while taking reverse.
Further, it is not the case of respondent No.1 that, the accident is caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending Tata ACE Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-02-TD-0966 and there was no negligence on the part of the pedestrian/petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to self negligence of the petitioner or else there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet, has clearly stated that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata ACE Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-02-TD-0966.

Admittedly,
the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata ACE Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-02-TD-0966 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 24-08-2022 at about 8.30 a.m., at Melapuram, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata ACE Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-02-TD-0966.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Ace Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-02-TD-0966 and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record, the petitioner has sustained compound fracture both bones of right leg (Type-3B) and for the said injuries she has underwent surgeries.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has not produced any relevant document.
In the petition, her age is shown as 43 years, as on the date of accident.

Likewise, in all the medical records, produced and got marked by the petitioner as Mahabunny vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189857663/

On the other hand,
the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident, is not specifically denied or seriously disputed by the respondent No.1.
Even, there is no contrary material on record, which creates doubt on the oral evidence adduced by the petitioner or on the documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is considered as 45 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered compound fracture both bones of right leg (Type-3B) and for the said injuries she has undergone surgeries i.e.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the above knee amputation of the right lower limb at the level of upper third of right thigh amount to 85% of disability and 42.5% to the whole body.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The above medical records produced by the petitioner clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered compound fracture both bones of right leg (Type-3B) and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgeries i.e. wound debridement with external fixation under popliteal and femoral nerve block, wound debridement and right above knee amputation,
wound debridement and revision amputation stump.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross- examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further,
he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner as assessed by him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

On the other hand, there is absolutely no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.1 to show that, the above medical records are false created documents and the disability assessed by the P.W.2 is wrong.

Therefore,
considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 42.5% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 42.5% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was working as tailor at Zaki Garments, Gowribidanur and was earning Rs.18,000/- per month.

Further, she has deposed that,
due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident she is unable to do tailoring work.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.

She has not produced any document to show that,
before accident she was doing tailoring work.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the Mahabunny vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189857663/

sentences.text: Hence, it is just and essential to include the future prospects to the income.
As per the judgment of Pranay Sethi, the petitioner not being a permanent employee and aged about 45 years, she is entitled to addition of 25% of the total income as future prospects.
Therefore, the future prospects comes about Rs.46,500/-.
Therefore, the total income including future prospects comes about Rs.2,32,500/-.

c) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 45 years is 14.

iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on her right leg i.e. compound fracture both bones of right leg (Type-3B).

As per Ex.P.8 to 10 discharge summaries and Ex.P.13 to 15 case-sheets, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 63 days from 24-08-2022 to 04-10-2022, 04-10-2022 to 11-10-2022 and 01-12-2022 to 14-12-2022, in Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru.

In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore,
taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.1 has deposed in her examination-in-chief affidavit that, she has purchased artificial limb for which she has spent Rs.2,00,000/- and the same requires to be changed once in every 3 years.

Even nothing with respect to same has been stated by the doctor/PW2.
Hence, in such circumstances this Court is of the opinion that, granting compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards future medical expenses could be just and reasonable.

opennyai_summary.arguments:

18. opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending Tata ACE Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-02-TD-0966 and there was no negligence on the part of the pedestrian/petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to self negligence of the petitioner or else there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident.
The investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet, has clearly stated that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata ACE Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-02-TD-0966.
Admittedly,
the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident Mahabunny vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189857663/
5 15.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata ACE Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-02-TD-0966 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
Further,
he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner as assessed by him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.
On the other hand, there is absolutely no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.1 to show that, the above medical records are false created documents and the disability assessed by the P.W.2 is wrong.
Therefore,
considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 42.5% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 42.5% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that,
before accident she was doing tailoring work.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.
